1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7.strategy: Puts the bishop on the long diagonal, pressing on d4, and prepares to castle. Black keeps every set-up open. The price is that White takes space in the centre first, and Black has to undermine it later.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Nf6.strategy: Develops the knight to its natural square and controls e4 and d5. Black commits to nothing, but White still has the first say in the centre and decides which structure arises.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6.name: Queen's Pawn Game: Rossolimo Variation
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6.strategy: Controls e5 and frees the c8-bishop, while the kingside pieces wait for later. The pawn commits the centre early: ...d5 now costs a tempo, so an early strike at White's centre is off the table, and White chooses the structure.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Na6.strategy: Heads for c7 or b4 and keeps the c-pawn free, but the knight stands on the rim and does nothing about the centre. Bxa6 can later double Black's a-pawns, though that gives Black the bishop pair. Sound, but White builds a strong centre on easy terms.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Nh6.name: Zukertort Defence: Kingside Variation
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Nh6.strategy: Develops the knight toward f5 and keeps ...Bg7 available. On the rim it does little for the centre, and Bxh6 Bxh6 gives Black the bishop pair, but White keeps the centre and builds at leisure.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 b6.strategy: Prepares ...Bb7 to go with ...Bg7, a double fianchetto that aims at d4 and e4 from the wings. Sound, but Black leaves the centre to White and has to undermine it later.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 c6.strategy: Prepares ...d5 with a solid pawn chain. It commits the c-pawn before White's set-up is clear. Solid, but passive: White can claim space in the centre.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 c5.strategy: Challenges d4 at once for a Sicilian- or Benoni-type game. If White takes on c5, Black regains the pawn but loses time with the queen; if White pushes d5, White gets a Benoni-style space edge. Playable, but White chooses the structure.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d5.strategy: Takes the centre at once. Black can aim for a solid or a counterattacking set-up, but for now only the queen guards d5, so 3.c4 attacks the pawn at once. Playable, but it commits the pawn before the pieces are out.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 e6.strategy: Keeps both central pawn breaks in reserve. No pawn contests d4 or e4 yet, so White can take the centre, and Black must undermine it later. Together with ...g6, the move leaves f6 without pawn cover, and the e6-pawn shuts in the c8-bishop.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 f5.strategy: Takes e4 away and aims for a set-up with the bishop on the long diagonal and quick castling. Playable, but White keeps a free choice of set-up, and the e6 square and the a2-g8 diagonal stay weak.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Nc6.strategy: Develops a knight but walks into d5, which attacks it. The knight cannot go to e5, where Nxe5 wins it, and every retreat loses time, so White gains space and tempo while the f8-bishop is still at home.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bh6.strategy: Attacks the c1-bishop, but 3.Bxh6 Nxh6 trades off the fianchetto bishop that the g6-pawn was meant to serve. Black is left with a knight on the rim and weak dark squares around the king.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 a6.strategy: Prepares ...b5 and ...Bb7 but does nothing for the centre or the kingside. White builds a full centre at leisure, and the queenside advance has no target yet.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 a5.strategy: Takes b4 from White's pieces and gains space on the queenside, but it ignores the centre and weakens b5. White builds a full centre with a free hand while Black has yet to develop.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 b5.strategy: Pushes the b-pawn before the pieces are out and leaves c6 without the b-pawn's cover. White develops pieces that attack b5, so Black must spend further moves to hold the pawn.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 f6.strategy: Takes f6 from the knight, leaves the g6-pawn without the f7-pawn's support and weakens e6 and the a2-g8 diagonal. It develops nothing, and White takes the centre while Black's pieces stay at home.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 h6.strategy: Stops Bg5 and Ng5 but is a slow, defensive move that does nothing for the centre or development. White takes the centre while Black has not yet developed a piece.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 h5.strategy: Grabs kingside space with ...h4 in mind, but the g6-pawn loses the h-pawn's support and the h-pawn can never again cover g5. White takes the centre while nothing of Black's is developed.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 e5.strategy: Drops a pawn: after 3.dxe5 the f3-knight guards e5, and once Bf4 adds a second defender, ...Nc6 and ...Bg7 alone cannot win it back. Black gets only a little development for the pawn.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 g5.strategy: Loses a pawn at once: the g5-pawn is attacked by the knight and the c1-bishop and defended by nothing, so 3.Nxg5 or 3.Bxg5 wins it and leaves the kingside open.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e4.strategy: Builds the full pawn centre and invites Black to attack it from a distance. White gets space and the initiative, but the broad centre is also a target for Black's pieces and flank pawns, so it has to be developed with care.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3.strategy: Mirrors Black's set-up with a fianchetto: the bishop will look down the long diagonal and the king gets a safe home. A quiet but flexible way to play, which leaves White the choice of a central break later or a slow build-up.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3.strategy: Brings the queen's knight out to back a later e4 and to watch d5. It blocks the c-pawn, so White gives up the c4 plan for a set-up built on piece play and a central pawn break. Black can meet it with a central pawn at once.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4.strategy: Develops the queen's bishop outside the pawn chain before e3 shuts it in. It is active and solid, but it leaves b2 without the bishop's protection, which a quick ...c5 and a queen sortie can try to exploit.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3.strategy: A modest, solid move: it supports d4 and opens the king's bishop for quiet development. The cost is that the pawn shuts in the queen's bishop and White hands Black time to hit the centre, so White plays for a slow, safe game.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.c4.strategy: Takes space on the queenside and fights for d5 from a distance, so White can still choose between a broad pawn centre and a patient set-up. It is a flexible way to meet the fianchetto: d4 stays well supported by pieces, and Black has to decide how to challenge the centre.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5.strategy: The standard reply to an early bishop: it hits d4, now attacked by the pawn and the fianchettoed bishop, and prepares a queen sortie against the loose pawn on b2. White has to settle the centre before finishing development.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 d6.strategy: A solid, flexible reply: the pawn takes e5 and c5 under control and prepares to develop the king's knight and castle. Black postpones the fight for d4 and leaves White nothing to attack, at the price of some space in the centre.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 Nf6.strategy: Develops the king's knight, covers e4 and d5 and prepares to castle. The knight blocks the g7 bishop's view of d4 for the moment, so Black trades the immediate pressure on the centre for quick, natural development.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3.strategy: Backs d4 with a pawn so that the centre holds against the c-pawn and the bishop on g7. White takes a solid but slightly passive set-up; the pawn also takes the c3 square from the knight, which will have to develop to d2.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.e3.strategy: Backs up d4 and frees the king's bishop, the familiar set-up with the queen's bishop kept outside the pawn chain. The b2 pawn has no guard, though, so a quick queen move to b6 makes White spend a tempo on it; the game stays solid and a little passive.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.Nc3.strategy: Develops a piece, but it takes c3 from the c-pawn, which was the natural way to support d4. With b2 unguarded, Black can open the centre and attack that pawn with the queen, so White is left defending rather than building.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3 cxd4.strategy: Trades the flank pawn for White's centre pawn and opens the c-file, so Black's pieces get play against d4 and the queenside. White keeps a pawn in the centre, but Black has the freer game and an easy target.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3 Qb6.strategy: Hits the unguarded b2 pawn at once, so White has to look after it before developing. The easiest answers are a queen move that guards the pawn or offers a trade, so Black gains a tempo, but the queen has come out before the other pieces.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3 Nc6.strategy: Brings a third attacker to d4, so the pawn is attacked as often as it is defended and White cannot simply leave the tension. Black develops naturally and keeps the exchange on d4 in reserve.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3 cxd4 5.c.strategy: The natural recapture: it keeps a pawn on d4 and opens the c-file for White's rooks too. White's centre is intact, but d4 stays the target of the g7 bishop, so development has to be accurate.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3 cxd4 5.N.strategy: Recaptures with the knight and keeps the c3 pawn, but the knight is then attacked by the g7 bishop, and a quick ...Qb6 hits it and the unguarded b2 pawn together. White has to defend accurately and is left with a slightly passive game.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3 cxd4 5.Q.strategy: Loses the queen for a bishop: the g7 bishop takes it and the knight recaptures, which is all White gets. The queen on d4 stands on the very diagonal the bishop controls.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3 cxd4 5.c.name: Queen's Pawn Game: London System, Pterodactyl Variation
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Bf4 c5 4.c3 cxd4 5.c.strategy: Develops the queen with check and gains a tempo: a knight that blocks on c3 is pinned against the king, and d4 comes under more pressure. The queen is out early, though, and White can chase it with natural development.

Adds a second attacker to d4, so White has to keep the lone centre pawn guarded and develop with care. Black gets a natural developing move and uses the open c-file and the long diagonal against the one target White has left in the centre.

Develops and prepares to castle while covering e4 and d5, so White cannot easily push the centre forward. The knight blocks the g7 bishop's attack on d4 for now: the pressure is postponed, not given up.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5.strategy: Hits d4 at once, the standard way against a quiet centre. The pawn is attacked twice and defended three times, so none is lost, but White has to decide how to meet the tension with a modest set-up.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 d6.strategy: A solid waiting move: the pawn controls e5 and c5 and prepares to develop the king's knight and castle. Black leaves the fight for the centre until White has shown its set-up, which suits the patient game e3 has chosen, but gives up the chance to hit d4 at once.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the king's knight to its natural square, covering e4 and d5, and prepares castling. The knight shuts the g7 bishop off from d4 for the moment, but White's quiet set-up gives Black no reason to hurry the pawn break.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3.strategy: The bishop takes its natural diagonal towards the kingside, and White prepares quick castling and a central break. White accepts a modest game rather than defending d4 at all costs, in return for a safe set-up.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.dxc5.strategy: Takes the pawn on c5, but it cannot be kept: the queen check recovers it at once. White ends up with a weakened centre and no extra pawn.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.c3.strategy: Supports d4 with a pawn, so the centre holds against the c-pawn and the g7 bishop with little effort and the pawn can recapture on d4 if Black trades. A solid, slightly passive set-up: the queen's knight has to develop to d2, and Black has the easier development.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 cxd4.strategy: Clarifies the centre: White must recapture, and the g7 bishop then bears straight on the d4 square. Black gets a clear target and open lines on the c-file in return for the central pawn.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 Qa5+.name: Colle System: Pterodactyl Variation
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 Qa5+.strategy: An early queen check that forces a developing reply. It gains a tempo, and d4 is only defended twice since the bishop on d3 shuts out White's queen, but the queen is far from home and Black has added nothing to the pressure on d4.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 Nc6.strategy: Brings a third attacker to d4, which White defends only twice because the bishop on d3 shuts out the queen. White has to react at once, by supporting the pawn or releasing the tension, while Black develops with threats and keeps the exchange in reserve.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 cxd4 5.N.strategy: Recaptures with the knight, which centralises it and keeps the compact e3 and Bd3 set-up intact. The knight is then attacked by the bishop on g7 and has to stay supported, so White's development must be careful.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 cxd4 5.e.strategy: Recaptures with the pawn and opens the e-file, keeping a compact centre with the bishops free to develop. The pawn is guarded only by the knight, since the bishop on d3 shuts out the queen, so the g7 bishop and a knight on c6 make it a target that White has to support.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 cxd4 5.c.strategy: Offers a pawn for development, but Black can simply take it and keep the extra pawn. White gets open lines and a quick knight on c3, which is not enough compensation against a solid position.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 cxd4 5.N.name: Colle System: Siroccopteryx Variation
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.Bd3 cxd4 5.N.strategy: Checks to gain a tempo while the g7 bishop already bears on the centralised knight. White can block with a developing move, and the queen has come out early, so Black needs a concrete follow-up to profit from the check.

Challenges the centralised knight at once: it is attacked by the knight and the g7 bishop but defended only by the e3 pawn, since the bishop on d3 shuts out the queen. White must trade, retreat or support the knight, and Black develops with tempo.

Develops the king's knight and prepares castling without committing the centre. It blocks the g7 bishop's attack on the d4 knight, so White gets time to finish development, but Black's position has no weakness and the half-open c-file is still there for later.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.dxc5 Qa5+.name: Colle System: Rhamphorhynchus Variation
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.dxc5 Qa5+.strategy: Wins the pawn back with tempo: the check forces White to block, then the queen takes on c5. Black has dismantled White's centre for free and has the more active queen.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.dxc5 Na6.strategy: Wins the pawn back with a developing move: the knight attacks c5 while the g7 bishop watches the long diagonal. White can take the knight with the bishop and double Black's pawns, but Black gets the half-open b-file and active pieces in return.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.e3 c5 4.dxc5 Qc7.strategy: Attacks c5 without a check, so White gets a free move to defend it. The pawn is hard to hold and Black keeps the more comfortable game thanks to the long diagonal, but the queen gains nothing over the check and White keeps more options.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5.strategy: Strikes at d4 straight away: with no pawn on e3, the pawn is attacked twice and defended twice, so White has to settle the centre at once.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 d6.strategy: Prepares to develop the king's knight and castle behind a solid pawn chain, controlling e5 and c5. Black leaves the centre alone for now, a patient set-up that suits the fianchetto bishop, since White's quiet move does not demand more.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 Nf6.strategy: Develops with a natural move, covers e4 and d5 and prepares to castle. The knight blocks the g7 bishop's view of d4 for the moment, but with White's king's bishop still at home Black has no reason to rush the fight for the centre.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5 4.Bg2.strategy: Completes the fianchetto and mirrors Black's set-up: the bishop looks down the long diagonal and the king is ready to castle. White allows ...cxd4 and recaptures with a piece, aiming for a quiet game with a sound structure.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5 4.c3.strategy: Supports d4 with a pawn, so that a trade on d4 can be answered with a pawn recapture and White keeps a centre pawn. It is solid but slow, and it takes c3 from the queen's knight, which has to develop to d2.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5 4.c4.strategy: Takes space on the queenside and fights for d5. If Black trades on d4, White recaptures with the knight and keeps a pawn on c4 against Black's centre, a set-up that restrains Black; the price is that the centralised knight becomes a target for Black's pieces.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5 4.Bg2 Qa5+.name: Pterodactyl Defence: Fianchetto, Queen Pterodactyl
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5 4.Bg2 Qa5+.strategy: The check uses the open diagonal to the king and forces White to block, but it threatens nothing concrete. White develops with the block and the queen has to find a useful square, so the early sortie is playable but gains little.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5 4.Bg2 cxd4.strategy: Clarifies the centre: White has to recapture with the knight, since the queen would be taken by the g7 bishop. Black trades a flank pawn for the centre pawn, gets a half-open c-file and keeps the knight on d4 under pressure.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.g3 c5 4.Bg2 Nc6.strategy: Develops with a third attacker on d4: the c-pawn, the knight and the g7 bishop hit it three times against two defenders. White must support it, release the tension or advance at once, so Black gets the initiative in the centre.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d5.name: Queen's Pawn Game: Chigorin Variation, Fianchetto Defence
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d5.strategy: Takes space in the centre and stops e4: the pawn is protected by the queen, so Nxd5 would win only a pawn for the knight. Black gets a solid centre and a fianchettoed bishop and meets White's set-up at once.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d6.strategy: A flexible, solid reply: the pawn takes e5 and c5 under control and prepares to develop the king's knight and castle. Black accepts that White can build a broad centre and plans to attack it later from the flanks and with pieces.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the king's knight and aims at e4, so White's central advance meets resistance at once. Black is ready to castle, and the knight blocks the bishop's diagonal only for a moment while Black decides between a quiet set-up and a pawn break.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4.strategy: Claims more space with a second central pawn, the usual set-up against a fianchetto defence. White controls d5 and builds a classical centre, accepting that Black will attack it from a distance with the king's bishop and flank pawns.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.e4.strategy: Takes the full pawn centre at once and leaves Black's fianchetto to attack it from a distance. White gains the most space, but the pawns on d4 and e4 need pieces to hold them, and the game turns on whether Black's counterplay can undermine them.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.Nc3.strategy: Develops a piece and adds control of e4 and d5, preparing the pawn centre. The knight takes the c3 square, so White plans a centre with the d- and e-pawns rather than a c-pawn space grab, and still lets Black's bishop take the long diagonal.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.g3.strategy: Mirrors Black's set-up with a fianchetto of the king's bishop, giving a safe king and a flexible, quiet position. It is sound but slow: White leaves Black time to complete development and claim a share of the centre.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Bg7.strategy: Completes the fianchetto and puts the bishop on the long diagonal against the centre. Black allows White the space and counts on counterplay against d4 and e4, which stay targets of the pieces and flank pawns.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Nf6.strategy: Develops the knight where it controls e4 and d5, so White cannot simply build the largest pawn centre without preparing it. Black keeps the fianchetto plan and decides later how to attack d4: with a flank pawn or with a central break.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Nd7.strategy: Supports a later central break with the e-pawn and keeps the g8-knight free to develop. The cost is passivity: the knight shuts in the c8-bishop and puts no pressure on the white pawns while White takes space at leisure.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Bg7 4.e4.strategy: Takes the full pawn centre and the most space. In return White has to take care of the squares behind it, since Black's bishop and pawns will attack the pawns on d4 and e4 and the position can become sharp.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Bg7 4.g3.strategy: Prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop, answering Black's set-up in kind, and to castle quickly. White keeps e4 in reserve and fights for the centre with pieces, a calmer plan that gives Black less to attack than the full pawn centre.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Bg7 4.Nc3.strategy: Puts a piece to work and adds control of e4 and d5, supporting a pawn centre without committing to it yet. White can still choose between building the full centre and a quieter set-up, depending on how Black arranges the pieces.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Bg7 4.e4 c5.strategy: Counterattacks the pawn on d4 from the flank, the classic way to challenge a broad centre. Black gets active piece play against d4, at the price of a position that is sharp and demands exact timing.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Bg7 4.e4 Bg4.name: Robatsch Defence: Rossolimo Variation
1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Bg7 4.e4 Bg4.strategy: Pins the knight on f3 to the queen, which weakens the knight's hold on d4 and invites White to settle the centre. Black keeps a compact set-up and develops the bishop outside the pawn chain, but the bishop can be harassed later.

1.Nf3 g6 2.d4 d6 3.c4 Bg7 4.e4 Nf6.strategy: The natural development: the knight attacks the unprotected e4 pawn and forces White to defend or advance it, while Black heads for castling with the fianchetto in place. Black accepts that White holds the broad centre and plans to undermine it once the pieces are out.
